AudienceIn.description:
How a client says who something is for.

Lives in core beside the rule, like `Page` and `CursorParams`: three slices
take the same three fields, and three copies would drift.
AudienceIn.title: AudienceIn

AudienceOut.description: Who something is for, as a reader sees it.
AudienceOut.title: AudienceOut

BulkCreateTrainees.description:
A spreadsheet's worth of trainees in one request.

The browser parses the file; the API takes rows. Capped so one request
cannot invite a whole university at once by accident.
BulkCreateTrainees.title: BulkCreateTrainees

BulkTraineesResult.description: Who was added and who was not, so a partial upload is not a mystery.
BulkTraineesResult.title: BulkTraineesResult

Capabilities.description:
What the caller may do, decided here rather than in the browser.

The B2B frontend keeps a table mirroring the backend policy and uses it to
decide whether to issue a request at all. Two copies of an authorisation
rule is one too many; this is the served answer.
Capabilities.title: Capabilities

CircuitConsole.description: One request for the screen a supervisor runs an examination from.
CircuitConsole.title: CircuitConsole

CloudSlotPost.description:
What the worker posts. `room_name` is fixed by `slot_payload_key` in its
own configuration, so the field name is part of the contract.
CloudSlotPost.title: CloudSlotPost

CohortCandidate.description: One candidate's standing in a sitting.
CohortCandidate.title: CohortCandidate

CohortSummary.description:
How a sitting's candidates compare, ranked.

Exam sittings only. A training circuit is people practising, and ranking
them against each other would turn practice into an assessment nobody
agreed to sit.
CohortSummary.title: CohortSummary

ConsoleStation.description: Null fields mean the version is not readable by this org, not that it is untitled.
ConsoleStation.title: ConsoleStation

CreateProgramme.description:
The exam this programme groups sittings under.

By code, resolved in the institution's own scope first: a school that has
written its own `plab` gets that one, not the platform's.
CreateProgramme.title: CreateProgramme

CreditSignup.description:
Ties the signed-in account to the visit that brought them.

Sent after registering, with the key the arrival was logged under. The
browser holds it; the backend never sees a partner cookie.
CreditSignup.title: CreditSignup

Dashboard.description:
Replaces seven calls on the SCA dashboard alone.

The legacy screen fans out to four RAG endpoints, a weekly trend and two
marketplace lists, then joins them in the browser.
Dashboard.title: Dashboard

DispatchAgent.description:
Which slot the agent is being dispatched for.

Named rather than taken from `active_slot_id`, so dispatching and switching
are separate decisions: a supervisor can re-dispatch the current station
without the circuit's state having to be right first.
DispatchAgent.title: DispatchAgent

GrantEntitlement.description:
An institution granting one of its people access to an exam it runs.

By email, as everything an administrator does is. `ends_at` left empty is
open-ended; an institution usually sets it to the end of the academic year.
GrantEntitlement.title: GrantEntitlement

LibraryStationRead.description:
A platform library station as it appears in a browse list.

Deliberately without `content`. The library is browsable by every signed-in
user, and the content is the patient brief, the examiner's context and the
marking guidance — reading it before sitting the station is reading the
answers. `version_id` is what a practice set or a circuit binds, so a
caller never needs the body to use one.
LibraryStationRead.title: LibraryStationRead

LogoutRequest.description:
The session to end.

Optional: without it every session ends, which is what "sign me out
everywhere" means. With it only the presented chain goes, so signing out on
a phone leaves the laptop signed in.
LogoutRequest.title: LogoutRequest

MySittings.description:
The trainee portal's whole screen, in one request.

It polls two lists every five seconds and joins them in the browser to
answer one question: is it my turn yet?
MySittings.title: MySittings

MySlot.description: A station this person is rostered onto, from their side of it.
MySlot.title: MySlot

OrgCounts.description: What the setup checklist counts. Four legacy calls existed to produce these.
OrgCounts.title: OrgCounts

OrgSetup.description:
Whether the organisation can actually hold a sitting yet.

Each flag is a step the browser was deriving from a list it fetched only to
take the length of.
OrgSetup.title: OrgSetup

QueueStatus.description:
Where someone stands, and what to do next.

`position` is why this is one call: b2c polls a status endpoint every three
seconds, and it should be able to answer "am I matched yet?" in one round
trip.
QueueStatus.title: QueueStatus

RebuildCircuit.description:
A circuit's new shape. Everything omitted is left as it is.

The trainees and the stations are sent whole rather than as a patch: the
slots are rebuilt from them, and a partial edit would leave the API
guessing which pairing the supervisor meant.
RebuildCircuit.title: RebuildCircuit

ReceiptRead.description:
A payment receipt, rendered.

Every field is a string already formatted for display: a receipt is read by
people rather than parsed by clients, and rendering money and dates in the
browser is how two surfaces come to show the same payment differently.
ReceiptRead.title: ReceiptRead

RecordArrival.description: Public: a visitor landing from a partner link, before any account exists.
RecordArrival.title: RecordArrival

ResolveRosterRequest.description: Who a circuit would name, before it is built.
ResolveRosterRequest.title: ResolveRosterRequest

ResolvedRoster.description:
Who a circuit would actually contain, and what is missing.

Returned before a circuit is built so a supervisor sees an empty linked
group now rather than when the examination starts.
ResolvedRoster.title: ResolvedRoster

ResultAcknowledgement.description: A candidate's confirmation that they have read their result.
ResultAcknowledgement.title: ResultAcknowledgement

SaveGpLeadReview.description:
`revision` is what the client last read.

Required, so a client that does not send it cannot overwrite blindly.
SaveGpLeadReview.title: SaveGpLeadReview

SetPlatformAdmin.description: Grant or revoke, spelled out rather than implied by which route was called.
SetPlatformAdmin.title: SetPlatformAdmin

SlotRagSummary.description:
What several reviewers of one slot agreed, or did not.

The worst rating wins per domain, which is b2b's tie-break and worth
keeping: when two reviewers disagree about a candidate, the lower rating is
the one that should prompt a conversation. Computed here rather than in the
browser so a supervisor's screen, a released result and an export cannot
each arrive at a different answer.
SlotRagSummary.title: SlotRagSummary

StartedAttempt.description:
What starting a set entry returns.

Deliberately this slice's own shape rather than `attempts`' response model.
They would look alike today and diverge the moment either contract moves,
and a client of one should not break because the other added a field.
StartedAttempt.title: StartedAttempt

StreamTicket.description:
A short-lived credential for one `EventSource` connection.

`EventSource` cannot send an `Authorization` header; see `core.streams` for
why this exists rather than a cookie or a token in the query string.
StreamTicket.title: StreamTicket

SupervisorCircuitRow.description: One circuit this person is named on, with the sitting it belongs to.
SupervisorCircuitRow.title: SupervisorCircuitRow

TrackingReference.description: What a partner puts in one link, and where that link points.
TrackingReference.title: TrackingReference

TraineeResultRead.description:
What a candidate sees.

Deliberately narrower than the internal record: moderation notes and the
evidence snapshot are ours, not theirs. b2b's own schema doc says not to
reproduce disclosure policy in frontend transforms — so it is applied here.
TraineeResultRead.title: TraineeResultRead

UpdateBrief.description: The one field a published version will accept a change to.
UpdateBrief.title: UpdateBrief

UpdateExam.description: Everything but the code, which existing plans and ref ids depend on.
UpdateExam.title: UpdateExam

UpdateOrganization.description:
What a platform administrator may change about an organisation.

Not the slug: every foreign key points at `id` and the slug is the URL, so
renaming one is a redirect problem rather than a field edit.
UpdateOrganization.title: UpdateOrganization

UserSummary.description: An account as the console lists it. No password state, no memberships.
UserSummary.title: UserSummary

VoiceGrant.description:
What the browser needs to join, and nothing more.

No agent name and no backend label: those are dispatch details the client
has no use for, and b2c currently hands the browser a metadata blob it
simply passes back.
VoiceGrant.title: VoiceGrant

WorkerBootstrap.description:
`{attempt, scenario}` — the only thing a worker is told.

Both halves are passed through as the engine's own documents rather than
re-modelled here: re-describing them would create a second definition of a
contract the engine already owns, free to drift.
WorkerBootstrap.title: WorkerBootstrap

WorkerSessionPayload.description:
`{"session": {...}}` — the shape `livekit_assistant_worker` validates.

Its paths are hardcoded in the worker rather than configured per backend, so
this API must mount them exactly. Noted in the README.
WorkerSessionPayload.title: WorkerSessionPayload

app__features__identity__schemas__Accept.description: Returned where the answer must not depend on whether a record exists.
app__features__identity__schemas__Accept.title: Accepted

post.description:
The candidate walks away before finishing.

Otherwise the attempt stays `running` forever, holding the slot's one live
attempt and counting as in progress on every screen that reads it.

get.description:
A page rather than one result: re-scoring under a new policy adds beside
the old, so a candidate's history stays readable.

post.description: Ends the presented session, or every session when none is named.

A sixty-second credential a browser can put in a stream's URL.

Minted with an ordinary bearer token, spent immediately on one
`text/event-stream` connection, and refused by every other route.

get.description:
Public: the pricing page reads this rather than hardcoding amounts, which
is how b2c's client and server came to disagree about what a plan costs.

post.description:
Apply one delivery, at most once, and only if Stripe sent it.

The **raw body** is what the signature covers, so it is read and verified
before being parsed. Declaring a parsed body parameter instead would hand
FastAPI the bytes first and leave the signature checking something else.

delete.description:
Your own, anyone's if you are a platform admin, or anything addressed
inside an institution you administer.

b2c's delete routes carry no decorator at all, so anyone can remove anyone's.

post.description: Idempotent. b2c increments a counter, so a double tap counts twice.

get.description:
Everything this caller may see, or one room of it.

Without a filter the answer spans the public pool and every institution and
group the caller belongs to, which is what a single feed should be.

parameters.description: Opaque cursor from a previous page
parameters.name: cursor

schema.description: Opaque cursor from a previous page

get.description:
The exams the platform offers. Small set, so no cursor is ever returned.

The consumer catalogue: platform exams only. An institution's own exams are
not here and never are — they are that institution's, not ours to publish.
See `/orgs/{org_slug}/exams` for those.

A platform admin sees the platform's drafts, because they are the person
writing them, and nobody else's.

post.description:
Credit this new account to whoever sent them, once.

Its own route rather than a step inside registering: `growth` sits above
`identity`, so registration cannot call it, and a partner who sent somebody
was credited with nothing at all until this existed. Null when there is
nothing to credit, which is the ordinary case.

Public: a visitor arriving from a partner link, before any account exists.

Unauthenticated by necessity — there is nobody to authenticate yet — which
is why the partner must be a known one and the visitor key is opaque.

get.description:
Checked against the partner in the path, so one partner's reporter
cannot read another's numbers.

The references this partner puts in its links, one per exam in the pilot.

Reporter-gated like the funnel: a reference is commercially meaningful, and
one partner has no business reading another's.

post.description: Platform admin only: partners do not appoint their own reporters.

get.description:
Open slots this caller may take: the public pool plus every institution
and group they belong to, or one room of it.

post.description:
Claimed once. The row is locked before it is examined, so the second of
two simultaneous claims is told the slot is gone rather than double-booked.

get.description:
One call for a screen that currently makes seven.

A read model over several aggregates. "Dashboard" is not a domain concept —
nothing owns one and no rule is enforced about it — which is why this slice
has no tables and no domain module.

Expired grants are included with `live` computed, because "your access
ended on the 3rd" is a more useful answer than an empty list.
The receipt ids for this person's payments, newest first.

One receipt, rendered.

Scoped to the caller. A receipt id is short and printed on a document that
gets forwarded to an accountant or an employer, so it must not be a key
anybody holding it can read.

post.description: One code per person; asking again returns the one they have.
Codes could be issued and never redeemed, so a referrer earned nothing.

get.description: Released revisions only, and narrower than the internal record.

post.description: "I have read this." Appended to the decision's event chain, once per revision.

get.description:
What a trainee is rostered onto, and whether it is their turn.

The portal asks two endpoints every five seconds and joins them in the
browser to answer that. The organisation slugs come from the caller's own
token, which already carries them.
The trainee portal, pushed. Replaces a five-second poll of two lists.

200.description: An SSE stream: `connected`, then a `snapshot` frame whose `data` is a `MySittings` each time the state changes, and `ping` every 25 seconds.

get.description:
Each set carries its own progress, so the list does not need a call per
station to work out how far along someone is.

put.description:
Change who is on a circuit and which stations they sit (C3).

A structural edit rebuilds the slots, so it is refused once one of them
means something: `circuit_locked` (409) if a consultation is in progress,
if feedback has been recorded, or if any station has already been run.

post.description: Add people to a training circuit, into the room it is already using.

get.description:
One request for the screen an examination is run from.

Replaces a session read, a station list, a trainee list, a staff list and a
feedback probe per slot — repeated every eight seconds while a circuit runs.

The console, pushed. The streaming form of the route above it.

Every frame is a whole `CircuitConsole`, so a client renders a stream and a
poll with the same code — and a missed event costs a reconnect rather than
a wrong screen.

Access is resolved once, before the stream opens, against a short session
of its own: this route cannot take the request session, because that
transaction would stay open for as long as the supervisor's tab does.

200.description: An SSE stream: `connected`, then a `snapshot` frame whose `data` is a `CircuitConsole` each time the state changes, and `ping` every 25 seconds.

post.description: Put an agent into the circuit's room for one station.

get.description:
Whether the slots may still be rebuilt, and why not.

Asked rather than discovered: the console needs this before it offers an
edit, not after somebody has typed one.

post.description: Stop the station without ending the circuit: only the agent leaves.

A supervisor runs the circuit they were assigned, so org membership is
the gate rather than admin rights.
Also starts the new slot's reading clock on the server (D-6).

get.description: The institutional home screen: counts, setup state and recent sittings.
What this institution has granted, revoked ones included.

post.description:
Grant one of this institution's people access to an exam it runs.

A trainee's exam-day slot never needs this: a dispatched slot skips the
gate. This is for practising between sittings, which otherwise runs out
with the consumer free trial.

get.description:
This institution's own exams, plus the platform catalogue.

`drafts=true` narrows to the institution's own rows, published or not: its
drafts are its own business. It never widens the listing to the platform's
drafts, which it cannot see at all.

post.description:
An institution's own exam, as a draft.

Written without asking the platform and without picking from a list: an
institution defines the exams it assesses against. The code is unique
within this organisation only, so two schools may both have a `finals`.

patch.description: Only this institution's own exams. A platform exam answers `unknown_exam`.

post.description: The institution's own call, on its own schedule. Refused without a rubric.
Stop running it. Past sittings and their results are untouched.
Publishes the template's newest version.

post.description:
Put somebody in this organisation, by the address an administrator knows.

An address with no account is invited: the account is created and the
person is emailed a link to choose a password. `invited` says which.
Revoked, not deleted: the record of who had access and when survives.

post.description:
Group this institution's sittings under one exam.

The exam may be the institution's own or one the platform published; the
code is resolved in the institution's scope, so its own wins a clash.

Preview who a circuit would contain.

A POST because it takes a body, not because it changes anything — the
alternative is a query string of repeated uuids.

get.description:
Circuits and slots embedded, because every screen that opens a sitting
needs all three and would otherwise fetch them one by one.

put.description:
Each save is a new revision. The table is append-only, so what was
previously considered survives.

post.description:
Release re-checks the evidence.

A station re-marked between sign-off and release would otherwise send a
candidate an outcome nobody approved.

get.description:
How this sitting's candidates compare, ranked.

What a GP lead opens after an examination to decide who to review first.
Completion ranks before score: a candidate who sat three of five stations
has a problem nobody has looked at, while one who scored badly has at least
been assessed.

Exam sittings only — `not_an_exam_sitting` (422) for a training one.

The whole sitting, per candidate: stations sat, marking, reviewers'
ratings and where the decision stands. Org admin only, because it carries
decisions that are not yet released.

put.description:
Institution admin only, and revisioned.

The revision the client last read is required, so two people with the same
screen open cannot silently overwrite one another.

get.description:
Every review of this slot, with what they add up to.

Not a `Page`: a slot has as many reviews as it has observers, and the
summary is about the set, so paging it would be paging half an answer.

put.description:
One review per person per slot, edited in place.

`mine` rather than an id: a reviewer has exactly one, and addressing it by
id would invite editing somebody else's.

post.description: Publishes the template's newest version, which stations may then be built on.
A new draft, seeded from the latest published version.

delete.description:
Throw away a draft. A published version is what an attempt was assessed
against, so it is archived instead, never deleted.

patch.description:
Correct the reading brief without cutting a new version (T5).

The brief is what a candidate is handed before the station starts —
presentation, not assessed content — so a typo in one does not invalidate
what everybody else was marked against.

get.description:
The circuits assigned to the caller, whatever else they can see.

Assigned, not visible: an administrator who supervises nothing gets an
empty list here and reads the sittings routes for the rest.

put.description:
PUT, not POST: the body states who is in the group. b2b has no
membership table at all and matches a label instead.

post.description: An address with no account is invited and linked in the same call.
A spreadsheet's worth of trainees. Duplicates are reported, not fatal.

One route for revoke and restore: they are the same decision, and two
routes invite one of them to be forgotten.
Joining twice returns the place you already hold rather than a second one.

get.description:
Position, how many are waiting, and the session if one has been made —
one call, because the client polls this every few seconds.

The streaming form of the route above it (ADR 0015).

The place in the product where polling cost the most: somebody is sitting
watching the screen, and the whole feature is how fast they get into a room
with another person. Closes as soon as the answer stops being "waiting".

200.description: An SSE stream: `connected`, then a `snapshot` frame whose `data` is a `QueueStatus` each time the state changes, and `ping` every 25 seconds.

post.description:
A new platform exam, as a draft — the consumer catalogue.

The table starts empty and stays that way until somebody writes one. There
is no seed: four exams used to be inserted by a migration and mirrored by a
tuple in this slice, and a fifth needed both changed and shipped.
Offer the exam. Refused until it names the rubric it is marked against.
Stop offering it. Past attempts keep working; nothing new may name it.

get.description: Every organisation on the platform. The console's first screen.

post.description:
Put the first person into an organisation.

Every other membership is added by an org admin, and a freshly provisioned
organisation has none: the console could provision, rename and suspend an
organisation but could not seat its owner, so the first row had to be
inserted by hand. A platform admin holds no org role, so this is the one
membership write that does not go through `OrgAdmin`.

Lift a suspension. Suspending had no inverse, and an action with none is
one nobody dares use.

Grant or revoke the console itself. One route, because they are one

The published platform library, which nothing could read before.

Every signed-in user, because the library is the product: a consumer builds
a practice set from it and an institution draws on it to build a circuit.
The rows carry no station content — see `LibraryStationRead`.

post.description:
A worker has connected, so hold the slot for a whole session.

Only lengthens a room that already holds one: a self-hosted session in a
room nobody reserved must not start being counted against the Cloud cap.
The session is over. Give the slot back before its expiry would.
The GPT-Live path reports usage and why the session ended.
